Explain the example for clean up a scene

blocks.text: GPU resources need explicit cleanup when a scene is no longer used. Stop its animation and dispose of geometry, materials and renderer resources.

Use a browser project with the three package installed and a module build tool. Each example creates its own canvas. Run one at a time. These library imports are not supported by this site's plain runner.

blocks.title: Clean up a scene

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `setAnimationLoop` repeats rendering through the renderer's animation system. Pass null when the scene should stop.
`dispose` releases owned graphics resources. Call it only when no remaining scene part needs those resources.
A perspective camera needs a field of view, aspect ratio, near distance and far distance to describe its view.

blocks.text: Calling disposeScene removes this example's canvas and releases its owned resources.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Only dispose resources when no remaining object uses them. Shared materials may belong to more than one mesh.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: List the resources this cleanup owns.
